ITEM.PTXT: The rear view monitor camera consists of an image input section using an ultra-wide-angle lens and an image signal output section consisting of a compact (1/4 inch) color CCD camera.

The image signal output section uses a CCD (Charge Coupled Device) image sensor to convert the image captured (input) by the lens into electrical signals according to light intensity, and outputs them to the back guide monitor computer.

The output image from the rear view monitor camera is itself reversed to match the view when looking rearward in the inner rear view mirror. Therefore, care is required because the image on the screen is shown laterally reversed compared with looking directly rearward (objects on the left side of the vehicle are displayed on the left side of the screen, and objects on the right side of the vehicle on the right side of the screen).

ITEM.PTXT: The "estimated course lines" indicate the steering angle when reversing; by reversing while operating the steering wheel so that the estimated course lines match the lines of the parking space, the vehicle can be guided into the parking space.

The "vehicle width extension lines" serve as a guide when parking straight within a space; by judging the relationship (intersecting → parallel) between the parking space lines and the vehicle width extension lines, it can be confirmed that the vehicle is facing straight into the space.

When parallel parking guide mode is selected, in addition to the screen display, guidance on the vehicle stop positions and steering operation timing is given at each point in the parallel parking process. Some of these are shown below.

LIST1.TITLE: Stop Position Guidance Before Steering Operation

ITEM.PTXT: After the vehicle is stopped at the initial position, the voice guidance "Back up until the green vertical line aligns with the rear of the adjacent vehicle, then stop. " is output. By reversing until the green vertical line aligns with the rear end of the adjacent vehicle according to the voice guidance, the vehicle can be stopped at the appropriate position before turning the steering wheel.

When the vehicle reverses with the green vertical line aligned with the rear end of the adjacent vehicle, a "green frame linked to steering operation" is displayed on the screen together with the voice guidance "While stopped, turn the steering wheel to align the green frame with the parking space. " is output. By turning the steering wheel according to the voice guidance and aligning the green frame with the desired parking position, the appropriate steering angle can be set.

When the vehicle is backed up following the voice guidance, a "green curve" is displayed; when the vehicle is backed up further until the "green curve" aligns with the edge point where the driver wants to park, the voice guidance says "When the green line aligns with the position you want to pull over to, stop and turn the steering wheel fully to the right. " is output. By then turning the steering wheel according to the voice guidance, the vehicle can be parallel parked in an appropriate position.

MECA.TITLE: General Precautions for Using the Back Guide Monitor

ITEM.PTXT: Do not rely excessively on the back guide monitor. Reverse carefully, just as with vehicles without a back guide monitor.

Never reverse while looking only at the screen. The image displayed on the screen may differ from the actual conditions, and reversing while looking only at the screen may result in a collision or an unexpected accident. When reversing, always use the inner rear view mirror and outer mirrors as well, and directly confirm that it is safe behind and around the vehicle.

Do not subject the rear view monitor camera to strong impacts or force. The camera direction may be misaligned, causing malfunctions. Special tools are required to adjust the camera direction, so always have it done at a dealer.
Use with the back door securely closed.
Do not use when the road surface is slippery (icy or snowy roads, etc.) or when tire chains are used. Doing so may result in a collision or an unexpected accident.

MECA.TITLE: Display Precautions Related to Vehicle Load and Road Surface Conditions

ITEM.PTXT: Note that, depending on the number of occupants, load conditions, road gradient and unevenness, errors may occur between the distances and course shown by the distance guide lines and estimated course and the actual distances and course on the road surface.
If there is a steep slope behind the vehicle, obstacles may appear farther away than they actually are, as shown in the illustration below.

MECA.TITLE: Display Precautions When Obstacles Are Three-dimensional Objects

LIST1.TITLE: Since the distance guide lines and estimated course lines are based on the road surface, note the following points when there are three-dimensional objects (walls, vehicles, etc.) behind the vehicle.

ITEM.PTXT: When the estimated course lines pass near a three-dimensional object, contact may actually occur even if it appears on the screen that there will be no contact, as shown in the illustration below.

Distance intervals differ between three-dimensional objects (vehicles, etc.) and flat objects (road surface, etc.) shown on the screen. As shown in the illustration, A and B are actually at the same distance and C is farther than A and B, but they appear on the screen in the order B, C, A, so reversing to the position of B on the screen will result in contact with the three-dimensional object.
On slippery road surfaces such as snowy roads, errors may occur between the estimated course lines and the actual course.
When there is a parking space line on only one side, the lines may appear parallel on the screen even though they are not actually parallel.

MECA.TITLE: Display Precautions for Using Parallel Parking Guide

ITEM.PTXT: Even when parallel parking with the parallel parking guide, the vehicle may collide with something depending on the operation method, road conditions, road surface conditions and vehicle conditions when parking; always drive while directly confirming that it is safe behind and around the vehicle.
Use the parallel parking guide when parking on a flat, straight road. Do not use it when the parking position is on a curve or slope. Doing so may result in a collision or an unexpected accident.
The space required for parking varies slightly depending on vehicle conditions (number of occupants, load, etc.) and road conditions (gradient, unevenness, etc.).

When the battery is replaced or its capacity drops, etc., "System Initializing" is displayed on the screen to indicate that the system is being initialized; touching the "Help" switch on the system initialization screen changes to the help screen, which explains how to complete initialization (turn the steering wheel fully to the left and right). When initialization is completed, the normal display returns.
If the tires are replaced with tires of a different size, the estimated course lines may become inaccurate.
When reversing the vehicle, always directly confirm with your own eyes that it is safe behind and around the vehicle. Never reverse while looking at the screen.
The range shown by the rear view monitor camera is limited, and objects near either corner of the bumper or under the bumper are not shown.
Since the rear view monitor camera uses a special lens, the distance intervals shown on the screen differ from the actual distances.

The screen may be difficult to see when sunlight or headlight beams shine directly on the lens, in dark places (at night, etc.), or when the temperature near the lens is high or low, but this is not a malfunction.
If the glass in front of the lens is dirty, a clear image cannot be obtained. Remove any water droplets, snow, mud, etc. that adhere to it.
If a high-intensity point (such as the sun reflecting off the bumper) appears on the screen, the smear phenomenon peculiar to CCD cameras may occur.
A phenomenon in which a trail extends above and below (vertically) a high-brightness point (such as sunlight reflected off the vehicle body) captured by the camera.
